open_questions: Centroid imaging to rule out a blended EB at ~50-66 arcsec
Higher-precision multi-sector photometry to test if depth stabilises with better aperture/correction
dossier.public_summary: The 13.1-day dip is about the right depth and flat-bottomed for a 3.7 Rearth planet, with no odd-even difference. However its depth more than triples from sector 64 to 102 (around 2500 to 8500 ppm) and even the four individual transits scatter far more than expected. Such changing depth is best explained by a blended or background eclipsing binary whose contamination varies sector to sector, not a steady planet on the M-dwarf. A centroid image would be needed to make the blend certain, but the variability is already positive evidence against a planet.

reasons.why: Depth changes strongly between sectors (2490 ppm sector 64, 6050 ppm sector 101, 8545 ppm sector 102). sector_depths_by_source verdict changes_within_a_source confirms real change, not just calibration.
Individual transits also inconsistent in depth (chi2 21.6 dof 3) despite only 4 transits. Combined with sectors this is positive evidence the signal is not a steady planet on the target.
No local centroid can place the dip on the target; neighbours could_cause 31 exists and neighbour blend is a viable false-positive given variable depth.
